```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.retina = 2,
  fig.width = 10,
  fig.height = 4
)
```

**grip** produces high-quality graph layouts using a multiscale force-directed
algorithm. This gallery shows what it can do --- each example includes the code
that produced it.

```{r}
library(grip)
```

## 2D layouts

### 8x8 mesh

The `"mesh"` preset produces visibly more uniform spacing than the generic
defaults on lattice graphs.

```{r mesh, fig.width=10, fig.height=4}
edges <- edges.mesh(8, 8)
default <- grip.layout(edges, n = 64, dim = 2, seed = 1)
tuned   <- grip.layout(edges, n = 64, dim = 2, preset = "mesh", seed = 1)

par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(1, 1, 3, 1), bg = "white")
grip.plot(default, edges, main = "Default", pch = 16, cex = 0.5,
          edge.col = "gray80")
grip.plot(tuned, edges, main = "preset = \"mesh\"", pch = 16, cex = 0.5,
          edge.col = "gray80")
```

### Level-3 Sierpinski carpet

The carpet preset keeps the recursive holes open and the dense interior well
separated.

```{r carpet, fig.width=10, fig.height=4}
edges <- edges.sierpinski.carpet(3)
n <- max(edges)
default <- grip.layout(edges, n = n, dim = 2, seed = 2)
tuned   <- grip.layout(edges, n = n, dim = 2, preset = "carpet", seed = 2)

par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(1, 1, 3, 1), bg = "white")
grip.plot(default, edges, main = "Default", pch = 16, cex = 0.4,
          edge.col = "gray85")
grip.plot(tuned, edges, main = "preset = \"carpet\"", pch = 16, cex = 0.4,
          edge.col = "gray85")
```

### Binary tree (depth 6)

The tree preset encourages more symmetric branching structure in force-directed
layouts.

```{r tree, fig.width=10, fig.height=4}
edges <- edges.kary.tree(2, 6)
n <- max(edges)
default <- grip.layout(edges, n = n, dim = 2, seed = 3)
tuned   <- grip.layout(edges, n = n, dim = 2, preset = "tree", seed = 3)

par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(1, 1, 3, 1), bg = "white")
grip.plot(default, edges, main = "Default", pch = 16, cex = 0.5,
          edge.col = "gray80")
grip.plot(tuned, edges, main = "preset = \"tree\"", pch = 16, cex = 0.5,
          edge.col = "gray80")
```

### 18-cycle

A circle initial placement with refinement recovers a nearly regular polygon.

```{r cycle, fig.width=10, fig.height=4}
edges <- edges.cycle(18)
default <- grip.layout(edges, n = 18, dim = 2, seed = 4)
tuned   <- grip.layout(edges, n = 18, dim = 2,
                        placement = "circle",
                        rounds = 64L, final_rounds = 128L,
                        num_init = 6L, num_nbrs = 8L,
                        r = 0.05, s = 4.5,
                        repulsion_factor = 1.25, seed = 4)

par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(1, 1, 3, 1), bg = "white")
grip.plot(default, edges, main = "Default", pch = 16, cex = 0.6,
          edge.col = "gray80")
grip.plot(tuned, edges, main = "Circle + refinement", pch = 16, cex = 0.6,
          edge.col = "gray80")
```

## 3D layouts (static projections)

The figures below use `grip.plot(projection = "ortho")` to show 3D layouts as
static orthographic projections from two different viewing angles.

### 8x12 cylinder

The `"torus"` preset also works well on open cylinders, recovering the expected
tubular shape.

```{r cylinder, fig.width=10, fig.height=4}
edges <- edges.cylinder(8, 12)
n <- max(edges)
coords <- grip.layout(edges, n = n, dim = 3, preset = "torus", seed = 5)

par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(1, 1, 3, 1), bg = "white")
grip.plot(coords, edges, projection = "ortho",
          azimuth = 35, elevation = 22,
          main = "Cylinder — view 1", vertex.col = "#1F3B73",
          edge.col = "gray80")
grip.plot(coords, edges, projection = "ortho",
          azimuth = -55, elevation = 15,
          main = "Cylinder — view 2", vertex.col = "#1F3B73",
          edge.col = "gray80")
```

### Level-4 Sierpinski tetrahedron

Explicit tuned parameters open up the simplex structure in 3D.

```{r tetrahedron, fig.width=10, fig.height=4}
edges <- edges.sierpinski.tetrahedron(4)
n <- max(edges)
coords <- grip.layout(edges, n = n, dim = 3,
                       placement = "barycenter",
                       rounds = 128, final_rounds = 192,
                       num_init = 12, num_nbrs = 16,
                       r = 0.07, s = 9.0,
                       repulsion_factor = 1.5, seed = 6)

par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(1, 1, 3, 1), bg = "white")
grip.plot(coords, edges, projection = "ortho",
          azimuth = 35, elevation = 22,
          main = "Tetrahedron — view 1", vertex.col = "#1F3B73",
          edge.col = "gray85")
grip.plot(coords, edges, projection = "ortho",
          azimuth = -45, elevation = 35,
          main = "Tetrahedron — view 2", vertex.col = "#1F3B73",
          edge.col = "gray85")
```

### 8x8 torus

The `"torus"` preset recovers the expected donut-like geometry.

```{r torus, fig.width=10, fig.height=4}
edges <- edges.torus(8, 8)
n <- max(edges)
coords <- grip.layout(edges, n = n, dim = 3, preset = "torus", seed = 7)

par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(1, 1, 3, 1), bg = "white")
grip.plot(coords, edges, projection = "ortho",
          azimuth = 35, elevation = 22,
          main = "Torus — view 1", vertex.col = "#1F3B73",
          edge.col = "gray80")
grip.plot(coords, edges, projection = "ortho",
          azimuth = -60, elevation = 40,
          main = "Torus — view 2", vertex.col = "#1F3B73",
          edge.col = "gray80")
```

global placement, the algorithm iteratively introduces and refines vertices
until the layout converges.

## Real-data showcase

### Zachary karate club

The karate club network (34 vertices, 78 edges) is a classic social network
benchmark. The 3D layout is colored by the known Mr. Hi / Officer faction split.

```{r karate, fig.width=10, fig.height=4.5}
karate.edges <- as.matrix(utils::read.csv(
  system.file("extdata", "karate-club-edges.csv", package = "grip"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
))
karate.n <- max(karate.edges)

karate.labels <- utils::read.csv(
  system.file("extdata", "karate-club-membership.csv", package = "grip"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
karate.labels <- karate.labels[order(karate.labels$vertex), ]
karate.club <- karate.labels$club
karate.cols <- ifelse(karate.club == "Mr. Hi", "#1b9e77", "#d95f02")

coords <- grip.layout(karate.edges, n = karate.n, dim = 3,
                       preset = "tree", seed = 10)

par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(1, 1, 3, 1), bg = "white")
grip.plot(coords, karate.edges, projection = "ortho",
          azimuth = 35, elevation = 22,
          vertex.col = karate.cols, edge.col = "gray80",
          main = "Karate club — view 1")
grip.plot(coords, karate.edges, projection = "ortho",
          azimuth = -45, elevation = 28,
          vertex.col = karate.cols, edge.col = "gray80",
          main = "Karate club — view 2")
legend("bottomleft", legend = c("Mr. Hi", "Officer"),
       col = c("#1b9e77", "#d95f02"), pch = 16, bty = "n", cex = 0.9)
```

### HMP microbial network (1,828 vertices)

This coarsened microbial co-occurrence network from the Human Microbiome Project
is the largest bundled example. The layout is colored by community state type
(CST), using precomputed results to keep the gallery fast.

```{r hmp, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
data(hmp.u01.gc.coarse)

hmp.results <- readRDS(system.file(
  "extdata", "hmp_u01_gc_coarse", "vignette_results.rds",
  package = "grip"
))

edge.matrix.from.adj <- function(adj.list) {
  edges <- list()
  idx <- 0L
  for (u in seq_along(adj.list)) {
    nbrs <- adj.list[[u]]
    nbrs <- nbrs[nbrs > u]
    if (!length(nbrs)) next
    for (v in nbrs) {
      idx <- idx + 1L
      edges[[idx]] <- c(u, v)
    }
  }
  do.call(rbind, edges)
}

hmp.edges <- edge.matrix.from.adj(hmp.u01.gc.coarse$adj_list)
hmp.cst   <- hmp.u01.gc.coarse$vertex_data$cst
cst.levels <- sort(unique(hmp.cst))
cst.cols   <- setNames(grDevices::hcl.colors(length(cst.levels), "Dark 3"),
                        cst.levels)
hmp.cst.col <- cst.cols[hmp.cst]

best.name <- hmp.results$top_local_candidates[[1L]]
best.coords <- hmp.results$layouts$local[[best.name]]

par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(1, 1, 3, 1), bg = "white")
grip.plot(best.coords, hmp.edges, projection = "ortho",
          azimuth = 35, elevation = 22,
          vertex.col = hmp.cst.col, edge.col = "gray85",
          main = "HMP network — view 1")
grip.plot(best.coords, hmp.edges, projection = "ortho",
          azimuth = -50, elevation = 30,
          vertex.col = hmp.cst.col, edge.col = "gray85",
          main = "HMP network — view 2")
legend("bottomleft", legend = cst.levels, col = cst.cols, pch = 16,
       bty = "n", cex = 0.7, title = "CST")
```
